findings.title: `DMDYRSUS` may use numeric codes for missing values.
findings.detail: Found 99 (2×): above every other value (the largest is 77), far beyond the rest, with nothing between. These are conventional codes for a missing answer, and nothing in the numbers separates a code from a real extreme value, so the reading is a proposal. The table is an NHANES export, whose codebooks define 7 and 9 (and 77/99, 777/999 in wider questions) as 'Refused' and 'Don't know'.
findings.why_it_matters: Survey and clinical exports code missing answers as 999, -9, or 7/8/9 in coded questions. Left as numbers they are averaged into your results; recoded wrongly, they remove real extreme values.

repairs.label: Treat as missing
repairs.consequence: `2` cells of `99` in `DMDYRSUS` become blank; the mean moves `8.86` → `6.25`.
repairs.sentence: `99` in `DMDYRSUS` was read as a code for a missing answer; `2` cells were recoded as missing on the user's instruction.

findings.title: Adjusting for total energy decides what a nutrient's coefficient means.
findings.detail: `DR1TKCAL` is total energy. `DR1TPROT`, `DR1TCARB`, `DR1TSUGR`, `DR1TFIBE`, `DR1TTFAT` and 18 more carry energy, and each correlates 0.31 to 0.91 with `DR1TKCAL`.
findings.why_it_matters: Adjusting for total energy makes a nutrient's coefficient a substitution: more of it in place of other energy at the same total. Leaving energy out, or partitioning it, asks about adding energy instead. The two answer different questions (Tomova et al. 2022), so which to ask is the study's choice and the method follows from it. For prediction, models that keep total energy predict alike.

evidence.source: research/NUTRITION_PACK.md#04 · Energy adjustment — the methodological signature

findings.summary: `DR1TTFAT` correlates 0.91 with `DR1TKCAL` across all `300` rows: nutrient effects are tangled with total energy.

findings.title: Use the dietary weights, not the examination weight.
findings.detail: This table carries `WTDRD1`, `WTDR2D` and `WTMEC2YR`. Dietary analyses take the dietary weights: `WTDRD1` for day-1 analyses and `WTDR2D` for anything using both days. They add adjustments for recall non-response and for the deliberate weekday/weekend allocation of recall days that the examination weight does not carry. `WTMEC2YR` is the examination weight and is not the right one here.
findings.why_it_matters: Unweighted or wrongly-weighted estimates are biased toward the oversampled groups, because NHANES deliberately oversamples specific race, age and income groups — so an unweighted mean is not a US-population mean.
findings.summary: Dietary analyses use `WTDRD1` and `WTDR2D`, not `WTMEC2YR`; as design columns neither becomes a predictor.

findings.title: The days in `DR1TKCAL` are not settled.
findings.detail: `DR1TKCAL` is in kcal, but how many days each value spans is not settled: its median, 1,868, is an adult's day's intake (a child's total over two days sits there too). Read as one day's intake, 3 of 165 rows fall outside 500–5,000 kcal; read as a total over 2 days, 14 fall outside 1,000–10,000 kcal. Which rows are implausible depends on it, so none is counted as a misreport until it is recorded, and the intake screens wait for it. Observed range 400 to 5,709, median 1,868.
findings.why_it_matters: These are possible days and poor estimates: a recall of 300 kcal is under-reporting rather than starvation. Excluding them is an eligibility criterion, which changes N and is reported in participant flow — so it is offered here and never applied. Nothing is filtered unless you say so.
findings.summary: Read as one day's intake, `3` of `165` rows fall outside `500`–`5,000`: record `DR1TKCAL`'s days first.

findings.title: `6` groups of columns look like repeated measures.
findings.detail: DRQSD (13: DRQSDT1, DRQSDT10, DRQSDT11…); DR1TVB (4: DR1TVB1, DR1TVB12, DR1TVB2…); DR1TS0 (3: DR1TS040, DR1TS060, DR1TS080…).
findings.why_it_matters: Wide repeated measures are fine for prediction, but if each row is a subject measured several times you may want one row per measurement instead — and clustered rows need a group-aware split.
findings.summary: `DRQSDT1`, `DRQSDT10` and 11 more look like repeated measures of one quantity, and 5 more groups. No control for this yet.

methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
methods.sound: Valid but wasteful, and a new row with a blank cannot be scored.

methods.label: Blanks as their own level
methods.customary: Customary for questions not asked (a blank medication answer)

methods.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)

below_detection.label: Censoring-aware
below_detection.customary: Less common in metabolomics; the epidemiology of exposures below detection (Lubin et al. 2004)
below_detection.sound: Sound for associations. Each non-detect becomes its expected value below the limit under a censored-normal fit, in each training fold without the outcome.

below_detection.label: Half the smallest detected value
below_detection.sound: Biased for associations as censoring grows, and collapses every non-detect to one value (Lubin et al. 2004: biased unless 5–10% are below the limit).

below_detection.label: As any other blank (the median fill)
below_detection.sound: Unsound: the median places non-detections in the middle of the distribution.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line

exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.
